regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY is the headline; GVA at 6.1% YoY is the economy. The 170bps gap is statistical discrepancy, not output. IIP at 6.7% YoY (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% YoY (down from 6%) confirm the deceleration that GDP flatters. PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led — manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 — which means the goods economy is softening even as the survey headline holds.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% — is the number RBI actually fears, not the 4.45% CPI headline. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is contained, which creates a dangerous illusion: the MPC may read the core as permission to ease, while fuel feeds into transport costs, logistics margins, and eventually non-food manufactured goods with a two-quarter lag. RBI's own inflation forecast has already been revised up 50bps to 5.1% YoY — the committee is telling you what it sees.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% — 75th percentile historically — only partially captures. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within four quarters, the taper tantrum forced an emergency reversal. Today's setup rhymes: NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% YoY (from 10.6%) signals wholesale funding is filling the deposit gap — and corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr/month (lowest decile) means capital markets are not a relief valve.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. against an RBI inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY leaves a real rate of 15bps — thin enough to be irrelevant as an anchor. The RBI is not cutting, but it is not tightening either, which means the INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) is doing the tightening by default. For housing, an average home loan rate of 8.32% p.a. against nominal GDP of 7.8% YoY means the real cost of mortgage debt is positive and rising — affordability is eroding without a single rate move.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) is the most credible capex signal in the data — utilisation above 75% historically precedes private investment acceleration. Bank credit to industry at 20% YoY (from 6.5%) and to services at 22.9% YoY (from 10.2%) confirms the financing is flowing. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% YoY (down from 6%) means the physical infrastructure underpinning this capex — cement, steel, power — is moderating. The investment cycle is real; its durability depends on whether deposit growth can fund it.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr/month sounds like a demand surge — but at 71st percentile historically, it is solid rather than exceptional, and the YTD at ₹10,42,757 cr FYTD (14th percentile) suggests the base is doing work. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY are the more honest consumption signal: two-wheelers are rural and mass-market, and 19.7% growth there means the informal economy is participating. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) against personal loan growth at 16.2% YoY — urban consumers are borrowing but not swiping, which suggests stress at the margin of discretionary spend.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (lowest decile historically) indicates capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or NBFC stress. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — at 74th percentile — indicates headroom for capex without inflationary pressure. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY prior) show broad-based capex financing. PMI composite at 54.6 index (83rd percentile, rising 1 of last 2 months) confirms order book strength.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Domestic capex is self-sustaining; public sector capex is not the only driver. Expect 12-18 month earnings upgrade cycle for discretionary capex suppliers. Avoid defensive sectors — the cycle is accelerating, not decelerating. Position for 15-20% earnings growth in capex-linked names through FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates most aggressively when CU is 75-80%. This is the sweet spot before inflation forces RBI to tighten.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit All-Time High","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (rising 2 in a row: 29,845 → 31,961 → 32,297), at 92nd percentile. SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 in a row: 16.64 → 18.2 → 18.62), at 93rd percentile. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 in a row: 82.03 → 85.76 → 87.08), at 86th percentile. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (rising 2 in a row: 128 → 8,930 → 58,502), at 100th percentile — highest on record. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn), at 82nd percentile.","implication":"Retail equity participation is at generational highs. Allocate to quality mid-caps with 15-20% earnings CAGR; avoid speculative small-caps. DII strength indicates domestic institutional confidence — use this window to reduce FII concentration risk.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile have historically preceded 12-18 month periods of mid-cap outperformance. Last time SIP AUM grew this fast (2021), mid-caps delivered 35%+ returns.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior month), at 95th percentile — the highest decile. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY prior) remains sticky. Brent crude at 97.47 $/bbl (flat, 69th percentile) and WTI at 91.52 $/bbl (flat, 77th percentile) are elevated. Natural gas at 3.181 $/MMBtu (up from 2.9 → 2.91 → 2.88 → 2.83 → 3.18 → 3.19, rising 3 of last 5), at 20th percentile but trending up. RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY (from 4.6% YoY prior).","implication":"RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation stays above 20%. Hedge energy exposure via long crude positions or energy stocks. Avoid rate-sensitive sectors (autos, discretionary) until fuel inflation moderates below 15%. Monitor geopolitical risk in Middle East — a 10% crude spike would push CPI to 5.5%+, forcing RBI to hold or hike. Position for stagflation risk: long energy, short rate-sensitive durables.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded 6-9 month periods of RBI hawkishness. In 2022, fuel inflation above 20% delayed rate cuts by 4-6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry Trade Slowly","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a.), at 86th percentile — highest in 17 years. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% p.a.), at 59th percentile. Fed funds rate flat at 3.63% p.a., at 67th percentile. US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (flat, 90th percentile). DXY at 101.114 index (up from 100.2 → 100.2 → 100.3 → 100.4 → 100.6 → 101.2, rising 4 of last 5), at 53rd percentile. US PMI composite at 56 index (up from 54.5), at 84th percentile. US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%), at 49th percentile.","implication":"BOJ tightening is gradual but structural — yen carry trades will unwind over 12-18 months, not weeks. This supports INR and emerging market currencies near-term but creates volatility. Fed is on pause; expect no cuts until Q2 2026 at earliest. Avoid duration risk in US Treasuries — 4.96% yield is attractive but likely to stay elevated. Position for a 50-75 bps yen appreciation vs USD over next 6 months; hedge via long JPY or short USD/JPY carry trades.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ rate at 86th percentile has historically preceded 12-month periods of yen strength and carry trade unwind. In 2023, BOJ tightening led to 15% yen appreciation over 9 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite Strong Flows","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (up from 95.73 ₹ prior, rising 3 of last 5: 95.24 → 94.34 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15), at 91st percentile — weakest in 10 years. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month, rising 1 of last 2: -114 → -3,111.9 → 29,631), at 83rd percentile. India VIX at 10.345 index (falling 5 in a row: 13.17 → 12.29 → 11.39 → 11.25 → 11 → 10.35), at 5th percentile — complacency. DXY at 101.114 (rising 4 of last 5), at 53rd percentile.","implication":"INR weakness is structural, not cyclical — driven by DXY strength and BOJ tightening, not RBI policy. FII inflows are masking underlying rupee pressure. RBI will likely intervene via spot sales or forward guidance to defend 96.50 ₹/USD. Avoid long INR positions; hedge via long USD or short INR forwards. For exporters, lock in 96-97 ₹/USD rates now. For importers, expect 97-98 ₹/USD by Q2 FY27 if DXY stays above 101.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness has historically preceded 6-12 month periods of RBI intervention and capital controls tightening. In 2022-23, INR weakness above 80 ₹/USD led to RBI FX swap auctions and import duty hikes.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Collapse Masks GCC Real Estate Shift","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (down from 13.65 mn sq ft / quarter, at 6th percentile — lowest decile), reversing a 6-month collapse: 21.5 → 26.9 → 48 → 29.9 → 26.9 → 13.2. Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 15.1%, at 42nd percentile). Yet Nifty IT at flat performance (Nifty 23,447, at 75th percentile) despite office absorption cratering. Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (down from 6.63%, at 8th percentile — lowest on record), rising 2 of last 5: 11.15 → 5.7 → 11.15 → 11.9 → 11.15 → 5.7. Rent in Bengaluru at 163 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 148 ₹/sqft/mo, at 95th percentile, rising 2 of last 5). Rent in Mumbai at 335 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 322 ₹/sqft/mo, at 100th percentile, rising 2 of last 5).","implication":"Office absorption collapse is NOT a demand crisis — it's a GCC (Global Capability Centre) shift from traditional IT services to tech-enabled back-office. GCCs occupy smaller, flex-space footprints in Tier-2 cities (Pune, Hyderabad, Bangalore suburbs), not Grade-A Mumbai/Delhi towers. Retail mall recovery (5% vacancy, all-time low) signals affluent consumption is ACCELERATING, not slowing. This decouples commercial real estate from IT services stocks. Action: (1) Overweight retail REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) — they're pricing office doom but retail is booming. (2) Underweight Nifty IT — office weakness is structural, not cyclical. (3) Long Tier-2 office developers (Prestige, Lodha) — they're capturing GCC migration. Falsifiable: If Nifty IT earnings grow > 15% CAGR next 2 years despite office absorption staying < 15 mn sq ft / quarter, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year low, but retail vacancy at 8th percentile is a 10-year high — the divergence is unprecedented. This signals a structural shift in real estate demand, not a cyclical downturn.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, 6.1% GVA — Services Papering Over a Goods Slowdown

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile); GVA at 6.1% YoY — the 170bps gap is statistical discrepancy, not real output.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 index (83rd percentile) is services-driven; Manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 index (48th percentile).
  • IIP at 6.7% YoY (down from 8.8% YoY) and Core Sector at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% YoY) confirm goods-economy deceleration.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY signal rural and urban consumption holding — the informal economy is not rolling over.

The tension: The GDP headline and the PMI survey say expansion; IIP, core sector, and the GVA-GDP gap say the physical economy is losing altitude. Services are carrying a load the goods sector is quietly setting down.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods — if it sustains above 10% YoY for two more months, the capex cycle is self-reinforcing; below that, the GDP headline becomes a trapdoor.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US PMI at 84th Percentile, US GDP at 49th — Survey and Reality Diverge

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 56 index (84th percentile, up from 54.5) signals re-acceleration; US GDP SAAR at 1.5% SAAR (49th percentile, down from 2.1% SAAR) says the opposite.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) is tightening financial conditions for the Fed — the bond market is doing what the FOMC has not.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, highest in 17 years) is unwinding the yen carry trade; DXY at 101.1 index (rising 4 of last 5 sessions) reflects the dollar bid.
  • But China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0% YoY) with PMI at 49.5 index (contraction) removes the commodity reflation backstop that EM bulls are counting on.

The tension: DM survey data is pricing a growth re-acceleration that nominal GDP growth and bond yields are simultaneously pricing as unsustainable. China's contraction prevents commodity prices from validating the optimism.

Bottom line: BOJ is the underappreciated tail risk — each 25bps hike unwinds carry positions that have funded EM equity inflows, including India's ₹29,631 cr/month FII bid.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Record DII Flows Meet a Deposit Gap That Cannot Fund Them Both

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr/month (92nd percentile, rising 2 in a row); DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr/month (100th percentile — highest on record).
  • FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr/month (83rd percentile), recovering from net selling three sessions prior — flows are positive but volatile.
  • But bank deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit growth at 17.1% YoY — a 630bps divergence — means the same household savings funding SIPs are not reaching bank balance sheets.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr/month (lowest decile historically) confirms capital markets are not absorbing the credit overflow.

The tension: Equity liquidity is at record highs; banking system liquidity is structurally strained. The household is allocating to mutual funds, not deposits — which is rational for the saver and dangerous for the CD ratio.

Bottom line: If deposit growth does not recover to 13%+ YoY within two quarters, expect RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights — which reprices bank credit and compresses NIMs simultaneously.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Mumbai Rents at All-Time Highs, Office Absorption at 10-Year Lows — A Market in Two Minds

The facts:

  • Mumbai office rents at ₹335/sqft/mo (100th percentile, up from ₹322/sqft/mo); Bengaluru rents at ₹163/sqft/mo (95th percentile, up from ₹148/sqft/mo).
  • But office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft/quarter (6th percentile — lowest decile), down from 26.9 mn sq ft/quarter — a collapse that GCC occupiers (42% of demand) are driving.
  • Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (8th percentile — lowest on record), signalling consumer-facing real estate is tightening even as office demand evaporates.
  • Office REITs pricing the divergence: Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit (down from ₹437/unit), Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down from ₹505/unit) — the market has already voted.

The tension: Rents are at all-time highs because existing occupiers are renewing at premium rates; new absorption is at decade lows because GCC hiring has stalled. The rent signal is backward-looking; the absorption signal is forward-looking.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 20 mn sq ft/quarter — the rent premium is a lagging indicator, and the REIT price declines suggest the market already knows it.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Fuel, Rupee, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) — if Brent sustains above $97/bbl, RBI's 5.1% YoY inflation forecast becomes a floor, not a ceiling, eliminating any rate-cut optionality.
  • INR at 96.15 (91st percentile, weakest in 10 years) with India VIX at 10.3 index (5th percentile) — complacency is priced in precisely when the currency is most vulnerable to a DXY spike.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. unwinding carry: each 25bps hike historically triggers 2–3% EM currency depreciation within 60 days — INR has no buffer at current real rates.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY — if wholesale funding costs rise 50bps, NBFC margins compress and credit growth stalls, threatening the capex cycle.

The tension: All four risks share a single trigger: a DXY move above 103 index forces INR depreciation, raises imported inflation, locks RBI into a hold, and tightens wholesale funding simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch DXY — a sustained break above 103 index this week activates the INR-inflation-funding chain and forces a reassessment of every rate-sensitive position in the portfolio.

"}
